newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HAGEMEYER REPEATS FORECAST OF HIGHER '96.
newsitem.headline: HAGEMEYER REPEATS FORECAST OF HIGHER '96.

text.p: Trading company Hagemeyer NV said on Thursday it maintained its earlier forecast that 1996 full-year earnings per share would show an improvement over 1995's.

"For the second half of the year consumer behaviour and developments in our markets remain difficult to predict," the company, which is about 37 percent owned by Hong Kong's First Pacific Co , said in a statement.
"Nevertheless, we maintain our previously announced expectation of improved earnings per share for the full year as compared with 1995," it added.
Last year Hagemeyer posted a total group full-year profit of 193.3 million guilders or 5.90 guilders per share.
In the first half of 1996 total net profit surged by 57.4 percent to 111.3 million guilders and earnings per share rose 12.3 percent to 2.36 guilders.
"This was achieved against the background of a 37.1 percent increase in the weighted average number of shares outstanding," the company said.
It added its Consumer and Professional Products division had faced difficult trading conditions in some of its markets but its overall performance was satisfactory.
"In Consumer Electronics, however, performance continued to be weak, especially in North America," Hagemeyer said. This was partially offset by good results from subsidiary Case Logic.
The group's Electrotechnical Materials division was affected by harsh winter conditions and lagging construction markets in the Netherlands and the west of Germany in particular.
Hagemeyer's Specialty Food activities showed good growth in sales, both organic and through takeovers, but its earnings were lower because of investments in warehousing and logistics.
Automotive and Industrial Products combined strong sales growth with good operating profits, Hagemeyer said.
